## Structure and components

- [statement] Duplo says the DC-648 camera scans barcodes and registration marks; job preparation and mark handling are part of the automation workflow. (low confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-648-slitter-cutter-creaser/ · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The DC-ST100 brochure distinguishes automatic changeover for one to three stacks across from semi-automatic changeover for four or five. Its automation claim therefore has a layout-dependent limit. (low confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/DC-ST100-In-Line-Stacker-Brochure_0326.pdf · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation
- [statement] The Uchida AeroCut nano operation manual warns that the machine cannot detect a double feed occurring with the first fed sheet. Double-feed detection alone therefore does not establish complete-deck integrity. (low confidence) — https://www.mybinding.com/cdn/shop/files/AEROCUT-NANO-operation-manual.pdf · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation
- [statement] Equipment dealer/service provider Print & Finishing Solutions says heavy static charge can cause misfeeds, double feeds or jams on air-feed cutters. Treat this as attributed service guidance, not a measured failure rate. (low confidence) — https://www.pfsgraphics.com/resources-slitter-cutters-trimmers · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Duplo describes the DC-648 as a single-pass slitting, cutting, creasing and perforating finisher for digitally printed sheets. This describes finishing automation, rather than evidence of a complete printed and boxed game. (low confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-648-slitter-cutter-creaser/ · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation
- [statement] The reviewed offerings advertise different output stages: AeroCut Nano cutting/slitting, Duplo batch stacking, and Rollem collation with downstream finishing options. Evaluate a proposed compact system against every required stage rather than treating card cutting or stacking as proof of a complete game. (medium confidence) — https://plockmaticgroup.com/morgana/product/aerocut-nano/?geo=us · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation · also: https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-st100-in-line-stacker/, https://rollem.com/machines/slipstream-iii/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MBM specifies the tabletop Precision Card Pro at 18.5 by 23 by 13 inches (depth, width, height); this compactness measurement applies to its slitter/cutter. (low confidence) — https://mbmcorp.com/product/precision-card-pro/ · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation
- [statement] Do not equate cutter speed with completed-game throughput: Duplo rates the DC-648 in sheets per minute, while MBM qualifies its card rate by letter-size paper and single-cut cards. Neither rating measures completion of the commissioned game. (medium confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-648-slitter-cutter-creaser/ · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation · also: https://mbmcorp.com/product/precision-card-pro/
- [statement] Duplo describes the DC-ST100 as supporting programmable batch separation and removal of completed stacks while operation continues. These features address output handling; they do not by themselves demonstrate correctly collated game decks. (low confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-st100-in-line-stacker/ · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation
- [statement] The DC-ST100 specification restricts paper weight to 230–400 gsm and maximum stack height to 40 mm; qualify the finished stock against the stacker as well as the cutter. (low confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-st100-in-line-stacker/ · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation
- [statement] Rollem describes the SlipStream III as able to cut, collate, punch and wrap in one pass, and says a deck can span multiple sheets. This is manufacturer evidence of integrated deck finishing, not measured performance for the commissioned game. (low confidence) — https://rollem.com/news/monthly-new-feature-slipstream-iii-collator/ · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation
- [statement] Rollem positions its AutoCollator for lower-volume or space-constrained applications, with cards presented downstream for punching, wrapping or packing. Its lower-volume positioning does not establish that every downstream operation is included in a compact unit. (low confidence) — https://rollem.com/processes/collate/ · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation
- [statement] In supplier-submitted material dated July 13, 2026, Rollem describes Cardistry as integrating slitting, cutting, collation, verification and boxing, rated up to 60 finished packs per minute. Treat the rate as a supplier claim; this article provides no independent game-specific throughput measurement. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-13) — https://www.packworld.com/coding-printing-labeling/package-printing/product/22970467/rollem-automated-card-pack-production-system · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation
- [statement] Historical operator accounts disagree about unattended finishing: in the November 2020 PrintPlanet discussion, Wheate valued being able to perform other cutting work while a Duplo ran; SoggyWinter reported recurring feeder attention to avoid double feeds. These are model- and shop-specific anecdotes, not current reliability rates. (low confidence) — https://printplanet.com/threads/duplo-finishing-machines.290798/ · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation
- [statement] Morgana describes the AeroCut Nano as an entry-level cutting/slitting model and says its cutters can be manually adjusted for specific job sizes; the specified machine dimensions are 565(W) x632(D) x963(H) mm. This documents a compact cutter with setup work. (low confidence) — https://plockmaticgroup.com/morgana/product/aerocut-nano/?geo=us · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation
- [statement] Duplo rates the DC-648 at a maximum of 40 sheets per minute and advertises slitting, cutting, creasing and perforating in one pass. This is a sheet-finishing rating, not a measured finished-deck rate. (low confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-648-slitter-cutter-creaser/ · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation
- [statement] Duplo’s DC-ST100 brochure, marked 0326, lists the connected DC-648/stacker dimensions as 126 by 35 by 47 inches. Floor-space planning should use the connected configuration. (low confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/DC-ST100-In-Line-Stacker-Brochure_0326.pdf · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation
- [statement] Rollem describes the SlipStream III as trimming/slitting sheets in two directions and collating them in one pass, with die-cutting, punching and packaging offered downstream. This explicitly describes deck assembly capability beyond ordinary card cutting. (low confidence) — https://rollem.com/machines/slipstream-iii/ · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation
- [statement] In its February 2018 installation announcement, operator NAPCO/Vulcan said its Rollem MK2 Slipstream could slit, trim, collate, stack, round corners, box and wrap inline. This is historical operator-reported capability, not an independent acceptance test or proof of a compact configuration. (low confidence) — https://vulcaninformationpackaging.com/napco-vulcan-introduce-playing-card-manufacturing/ · keywords: Compact integrated card production automation

This is a displayed equipment price, not a configured printer-to-boxed-game quotation; currency selection, tax, freight and installed-cost inclusions were not established.
